short: Her reign joined England and Scotland into a single kingdom of Great Britain.
full:
Anne came to the throne in March 1702 as the last Stuart monarch, having survived seventeen pregnancies without a surviving child. The War of the Spanish Succession dominated her reign, and Marlborough's victories at Blenheim, Ramillies, Oudenarde and Malplaquet made Britain a first-rank military power before the Tories ended the war at Utrecht in 1713.

The union was the constitutional achievement. Scotland's Act of Security had threatened a separate successor; English pressure and Scottish financial distress after the Darien disaster produced the Treaty of Union, and on 1 May 1707 the two parliaments were replaced by one at Westminster. Anne was the first sovereign of Great Britain, and the last to refuse assent to an act of Parliament, in 1708. Her reign also saw fierce Whig and Tory conflict and the beginnings of regular party politics. She died on 1 August 1714, and the crown passed under the Act of Settlement to George of Hanover.
